label: EXPERIMENTAL snowpack-structure prediction for expert decision support. Not an avalanche forecast, danger rating or operational guidance.
source: Avalanche Canada Mountain Information Network (public reports)

reports.title: Serac Ridge KNP (Mt -Verendrye north shoulder)
reports.comment:
incident: This report adds details to the avalanche incident already listed by Public safety.

Climbing along a ENE aspect burnt tree rib as a group of 5 friends,  around 2000m elevation, the second skier triggered a small soft wind slab in the freshly cut skin track.  The slab had a small propagation and slid on Dec. 2nd crust, catching and pushing two persons toward the north side on the rib 40d…

reports.title: Skier triggered avalanche on Serac Ridge Kootenay
reports.comment: avalanche: Skier triggered avalanche on Serac Ridge (Kootenay).  Suspect the failure plane was the Dec 2 persistent layer. Party of 5 was skinning up a steep ridge below treeline in a burnt forest and triggered a slab, 2 skiers involved, minor injuries and lost gear.  See Photos.

reports.title: Serac snow profile
reports.comment: quick: Test profile from 1800 m on Serac Creek, east aspect near the typical uptrack.

reports.title: Simpson 1 avalanche
reports.comment: quick: Wind effect at ridge top on many aspects. Nice powder below ridge top. Very faceted snow at lower elevations. Slab avalanche in open terrain beside trees. See avalanche tab. / avalanche: Suspected skier remote by another party that skied in the trees skier's left of the avalanche, where snowpack appeared to be shallower (the avalanche had already happened by the time we got there, but wasn'…

reports.title: Floe avalanche
reports.comment: avalanche: Remote trigger on east facing floe path on December 2 crust/facet combo. Significant propagation through burnt trees into adjacent gullies. Poor visibility so extent of propagation unclear but at least 3 gullies went.

reports.title: Several Na Persistent slab- 2150m, NE
reports.comment: avalanche: Observed from highway. Suspect triggered by small Nc. Unsure what layer the avalanches failed on but the crowns look to be ~70cm deep. Photo attached- apologies I have an older Iphone.

reports.title: Simpson Area cornice triggered slab
reports.comment: avalanche: Observed two fracture lines not seen on Friday.  Cornice triggers. Likely failed on late Dec facet layer

reports.title: Floe
reports.comment: quick: Lone party in Floe parking lot today. Skied from the top, stuck to the ridge for upper half of descent, skiers right of main slide path. Very reactive wind slabs on lee side of ridge, 20-30cm deep, size 1-1.5. Solid skiing.

reports.title: White Tail Burn
reports.comment:
quick: Spooky conditions in the White Tail Burn today. Snow conditions and the ability for recent storm snow to bond with the January 30th crust varied based on aspect. We believed that the North aspect may hold the best snow and found a mixture of hard slab (1F-), soft slabs (4F), and storm snow (F). Best ski quality existed lower down our first run. 

On our ski out, we observed a small release …

reports.title: Simpsons
reports.comment: incident: While skinning back to the car, first skier triggered a size 1 in the burnt trees, and was burried knee deep. We heard a womph a few meter before the incident. We skied a gully of similar aspect earlier, and saw no sign of stability.

reports.title: Vermillion Crossing
reports.comment: quick: Skied burned slopes near Vermillion crossing. 2* in the parking lot with rain. Conditions rapidly improved higher with snow steadily throughout the day. Ridgetop conditions considerably improved with lighter powder. Still a lot of buried hazards on the lower slopes. Hand shears found some failures in the Jan 30th layer but we could not replicate it in a ICT.

reports.title: Vermillion Crossing Avalanche
reports.comment: avalanche: Witnessed a skier trigger a size ~1.5 on a steep sparsely trees roll near Vermillion Crossing. Appeared to be a storm slab of variable thickness (perhaps as thick as 50-75cm in places?). Ran ~15m wide and 75m. Skier avoided involvement thanks to a rapid descent. We were not close enough to get an idea of the exact trigger site or other properties.

reports.title: Simpson Burn
reports.comment: quick: Lower slopes were wind affected, but we soon got to beautiful powder, up to 40cm near the top of the ridge on looker’s right. We travelled along the ridge but didn’t top out, choosing to stick below the alpine. Chose a beautiful rib to the skier’s right of the other tracks— beautiful fall line run—but avoided the gully further skier’s right which had fresh avalanche debris. Zoom in on the f…

reports.title: Serac ridge / remote cornice failure triggers deeper weak layer
reports.comment: quick: We were traversing from the south shoulder of Serac ridge to get to the far North end of the ridge (where there were less cornices and old deep avalanches, which gave us confidence in the snowpack). Upon getting to the ridge, we noticed an enormous crack immediately behind the cornice that heads off to the south; and due to this, we decided to keep as far away from the cornices as we reason…

reports.title: Observed skier triggered
reports.comment: incident: Observed an approx size 1 skier triggered from the highway while driving through. Appeared like ski tracks exited the path on skiers right. Hope everyone’s ok.

reports.title: Floe
reports.comment:
avalanche: We put in a ski cut at the top of one of the floe lake slide paths. This triggered few small sluffs which gained a lot of momentum as they traveled down the slope.

The resulting loose dry avalanche which traveled at least 300-400m down the slope and was somewhere between size 1.5 and 2 by the time it stopped.

reports.title: Small slab release at Whitetail
reports.comment:
quick: Multiple loud woomfs and one small slab released on backside of Whitetail. Issues only on W-SW aspect, everything else was very stable. Slab was 10-12inch thick sitting on a thin ice layer. Ice was not found in at least some other areas at the same elevation. 

5-10 cm new snow overnight, wet up until about 1600 m. Decently dry above. Slab was dryer snow. 

Spooky skiing on the backside. St…

reports.title: Hawk Ridge Test Profile
reports.comment: quick: We found 3-5cm of moist surface snow from valley bottom to 1800m, this new snow was overlaying a recently formed melt freeze crust. Above 1800m the snow quality improved and the near surface crust tapered. While setting an up track on a South aspect at 2200m we experience two large whumphs. We decided to dig a test profile (SEE PHOTO). We suspect the whumphs were failing on the Feb 16 crust…

reports.title: Healy Pass
reports.comment:
avalanche: Several point releases with wide runout on both avy paths en route to Healy pass. Not directly observed, but more added from in to out time. / snowpack: Feb crust down about 20cm on S aspect at 2200m. Not observed on N aspect at same elevation. Lots of settlement cones. 
Surface snow was light at 11, heavy by 1pm.

reports.title: Simpson Burn N Shoulder
reports.comment: snowpack: -9C on a NNE aspect. CTH 22 RP down 30 cm on surface hoar. CTH 28 SP down 50cm on melt freeze crust. Unburied surface hoar also observed on N aspects in burn.

reports.title: White tail
reports.comment: avalanche: Blue line was a 0.5 from an earlier group that had only ran down the sidewall of the gully. Yellow was size 1.5-2 snowboarder triggered. Crown was approx 60cm. Debris was 1-2m deep.

reports.title: Monarch Unskiable Terrain Avalanche
reports.comment: quick: Day time highs reached -3. Top level of snowpack only barely being affected by temps, little direct sun. / avalanche: Avalanche observed from a distance. Occurred in steep unskiable terrain. / snowpack: Compression test resulted in no failure.

reports.title: Low elevation avalanches in Kootenay Park
reports.comment: avalanche: Avalanche control surprise today in Kootenay on Simpson avalanche paths. Triggered smallish avalanches in the start zones that carried only surface snow down most of the path, but when the debris reached about 1800m, it began to pull 50 cm slabs off the sidewalls and onto the skiable terrain in the vicinity. Several of these propagations were >100m wide. Watch out below treeline in this…
